Naming and Shaming Walter Palmer

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We look into the naming and shaming of Walter Palmer the man who killed cecil the lion

Summary:
On the 28th of July the Telegraph published the name of Walter Palmer the dentist behind the hunt and kill of Cecil the lion.
Walter is an avid trophy hunter, he belongs to an elite hunting club based in NYC and has many trophies from his years of hunting. After his name was released and he started to become the most hated man on the internet, Walter released a statement saying he “thought the hunt was legal …. and he is sorry that he killed Cecil”
But the publics need for revenge didn't ease off. Fb hate groups were opened, people started pertitions to get him extridited to Zim, the address for his place of business was tweeted my Mia Farrow, his families places of business were published on the internet. Dr. Palmer had to close down his dentistry practice and seems to have gone into hiding, as the hatred for him on social media escalates.

Is naming and shaming part of the freedom of speech given to us by social media? Or is it mob justice that is destroying lives? We speak to writer and journalist Jon Ronson, the author of the New York bestselling novel, 'so you have been publicly shamed' about this modern day phenomenon

The Zim government has asked the USA to extradite Walter Palmer for his crime - the result of which may be known before we complete this piece.


Further information:
We will be getting all the details of Walter Palmer hunt from Johnny Rodrigues, of the Zimbabwe Conservation Task Force
The Zimbabwe Parks and wildlife management Authority will break down what his being accused of and exactly which park of the hunt is illegal
Cecil is the 25th collared lion to be killed by hunter in the past 10 years.

Press Release:


Trial by Social media
Lion killer Walter Palmer has faced a global public onslaught in what seems to have become a trial by social media. But the hue and cry over the death of Cecil the lion has resulted in drastic action and a revisit of trophy transporting policies and hunting regulations. Carte Blanche asks if social media is just a platform for armchair activists worldwide to name and shame, or if it has the power to be a modern catalyst for change?


Script:


Naming and shaming
Script #4

Cook report most dramatic scene footage

VO 1
Carte Blanche has been investigating the canned lion hunting industry for decades. As far back as 1997 our story on the Cooke Report caused widespread uproar. But that was in an age before social media. Over the last two weeks Cecil the lion has created a global outcry.
14”

Link – don’t read
On the 28th of July Walter Palmer’s name was released to the public, as the man who killed Cecil on a trophy hunt in Zimbabwe. Overnight the Minnesota dentist became one of the most despised people in the world.
• Montage of hate – global

2. VOICE OVER INTRO TO JOHNNY Johnny Rodrigues is the head of the Zimbabwe conservation task force
6”
Interview: Johnny Rodrigues
What happened on the 1st of July

Link 2 – don’t read
Public shaming through social media has become a way for everybody to express their opinion on those they feel have violated the rules. The public have become the judge, juror and executioner. Has this kind of virtual mob justice gone too far or is it just freedom of speech in the 21st century?

3. VOICER OVER INTRODUCTION OF Vasu
Professor Vasu Reddy is the dean of Humanities at the university of Pretoria
7”
Interview
Vasu: What is shaming? How has social media changed the game of shaming?

VO 4 - Pie charts and stats
Around 1 quarter of the global population - 2 billion - read the Cecil the lion story on social media. In South Africa, almost a full week after the story broke Cecil was still being talked about more by more than 50 percent of all those online. Globally South Africa only occupies just over 1% of the social media space. America dominates online activity. How has Cecil captured the hearts of the world?
29”




5. Voice over introduction of Sarah and Jennifer
Sarah Britten and Jennifer Jacquet are both Authors and specialists in Social media in particular naming and shaming
8”

Interview
Sarah and Jennifer
Why Cecil, why Walter Palmer?
Sam debose VS Cecil the lion

VO 6:
Most of the information circulating about Walter Palmer was leaked by on social media. We found these US Authority charging documents on Facebook showing that Dr. Palmer had paid past fines for hunting violations in the USA. For example, he hunted this bear in an illegal zone. Some of the information leaked has helped. But has some of it gone too far? Palmer’s holiday home has been vandalised, his daughters business details were posted online and after the address was leaked by Mia Farrow people began to protest outside his offices which were temporarily closed.
35”

Protest footage Footage
Upsound from Americans

Interview
Vasu: Human reaction to naming and shaming on social media
What power does it give the public and what does it take from the victim
Is it a case of the weak being able to defeat the strong
Sarah: talking about Sabrina and Kendal

VO 7:
last week Sabrina Corgatelli ignited a social media outcry after she posted pictures of herself with this giraffe that she killed while hunting in South Africa.
9”

Extract from the interview 18”

Interview
Sarah and Jennifer: outrage is useless of it doesn’t create change

VO 8: Conclusion
The social media naming and shaming of Walter Palmer has been a catalyst for dramatic change.
9”

VO 9: and text
1. Zimbabwe has banned trophy hunting around the Hwange national park.

2. Delta, United and American airlines have all banned shipping of big 5 trophies

3. New Jersey lawmakers are considering a ban on the import of threatened species

4. Democrat senators announced a new bill restricting the import and export of the big 5 trophies.
